record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: For problem (III), -Δu = K(x)(λu^β - u^α) in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, K(x)=1/d(x)^k, 0 < k < 2, and 0 < α < β < 1, and likewise for the p-Laplacian generalization mentioned in the paper, do compact-support solutions exist in the regime k-α < 1?

evidence.quote: (i) If k-α<1, there exists λ* such that for all λ>λ* there is a solution u_λ>0 to (III) and there is no solution for λ small; (ii) If 1<k-α<2 there exists at least a solution with compact support for all λ>λ**.
and if, also in this case, there are compact support solutions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ ($N\ge 1$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, and let $d(x):=\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)$. Fix real numbers $0<\alpha<\beta<1$ and $0<k<2$, and set $K(x):=d(x)^{-k}$. For a parameter $\lambda>0$, consider the singular semilinear Dirichlet problem
$$(\mathrm{III})\qquad -\Delta u \;=\; K(x)\bigl(\lambda u^{\beta}-u^{\alpha}\bigr)\quad\text{in }\Omega,\qquad u\ge 0\text{ in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\text{ on }\partial\Omega,$$
and, more generally, its $p$-Laplacian counterpart ($1<p<\infty$)
$$-\Delta_{p}u \;=\; K(x)\bigl(\lambda u^{\beta}-u^{\alpha}\bigr)\quad\text{in }\Omega,\qquad u\ge 0\text{ in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\text{ on }\partial\Omega,$$
where $\Delta_p u=\operatorname{div}(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u)$. A solution $u$ is said to have compact support if the set $\{x\in\Omega:u(x)>0\}$ is compactly contained in $\Omega$.

It is known that:
\begin{itemize}
\item if $k-\alpha<1$, then there exists $\lambda^{*}>0$ such that for every $\lambda>\lambda^{*}$ problem $(\mathrm{III})$ admits a strictly positive solution $u_{\lambda}$, and for $\lambda$ small no solution exists;
\item if $1<k-\alpha<2$, there exists $\lambda^{**}>0$ such that for every $\lambda>\lambda^{**}$ problem $(\mathrm{III})$ admits at least one solution with compact support.
\end{itemize}

Question: In the regime $k-\alpha<1$ (and analogously for the $p$-Laplacian generalization above), do solutions with compact support exist for problem $(\mathrm{III})$?
artifact.category_tag: singular semilinear elliptic equations with absorption
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located related work on positive vs. compact-support solutions for singular elliptic problems with strong absorption (e.g. Díaz–Hernández–Ilyasov and related papers), which establish compact-support existence under a "diffusion–absorption balance" plus a largeness condition on λ, typically in regimes corresponding to k-α>1. No source was found that resolves the existence (or nonexistence) of compact-support solutions in the specific regime k-α<1 for the problem above, so the status appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Positive versus compact support solutions to a singular elliptic problem
status_evidence.snippet: Studies positive vs. compact-support solutions for singular elliptic problems with absorption.
status_evidence.claim: Related results address the dichotomy between positive and compact-support solutions but do not settle the k-α<1 case.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of positive solutions and solutions with compact support for a spectral nonlinear elliptic problem with strong absorption
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes existence of compact-support solutions under diffusion-absorption balance and largeness of λ.
status_evidence.claim: Compact-support existence is proved in regimes other than k-α<1.
